skill.name: gene-database
skill.description: Search NCBI Gene and retrieve gene metadata using E-utilities and NCBI Datasets workflows.
skill.summary: Search, fetch, and batch annotate NCBI Gene records for research workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The high env_access findings are false positives caused by NCBI API key parameters and placeholders, not secret harvesting. Confirmed risk is limited to intentional outbound HTTPS requests from Python scripts to NCBI APIs. No prompt injection, hidden command execution, or malicious data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Outbound NCBI requests expose query terms to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external request behavior clearly and remind users not to submit sensitive unpublished gene lists without consent.

remediation.issue: API keys can appear in command history when passed as CLI arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Add support for reading the NCBI API key from an environment variable or an interactive prompt.

remediation.issue: The batch output option can overwrite an existing file path.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting existing files or require an explicit force option.

content.value_statement: Gene lookups often require repeated NCBI API calls and careful organism filters. This skill provides scripts and workflows for searching, fetching, and batching gene annotations.
actual_capabilities: Search NCBI Gene by symbol, name, disease, chromosome, GO term, or organism filter.
Fetch ESummary and EFetch records for one or more Gene IDs.
Retrieve NCBI Datasets gene metadata by Gene ID or symbol plus taxon.
Process batch gene symbol or ID lists with rate limiting.
Output readable summaries or JSON files for downstream annotation workflows.
limitations: Requires network access to NCBI endpoints.
Does not provide clinical interpretation, diagnosis, or medical advice.
Results depend on NCBI availability and API schema changes.
API key handling is optional and user managed.

use_cases.title: Annotate Disease Gene Lists
use_cases.description: Search disease terms and retrieve gene identifiers, descriptions, organisms, chromosomes, and map locations.

use_cases.title: Validate Gene Panels
use_cases.description: Batch check gene symbols or IDs before pipeline analysis, reports, or publication tables.

use_cases.title: Compare Model Organisms
use_cases.description: Look up the same gene across supported taxa and compare identifiers, aliases, and genomic locations.

prompt_templates.title: Search One Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to search BRCA1 in human. Summarize the Gene ID, symbol, description, organism, and chromosome.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch by Gene ID
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the NCBI Datasets workflow to fetch Gene ID 672. Return a readable summary with aliases, location, and transcripts.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate a Panel
prompt_templates.prompt: Use batch lookup for BRCA1, TP53, EGFR, and KRAS in human. Include status, Gene ID, symbol, organism, and map location.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pathway Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an NCBI Gene search for apoptosis genes in mouse. Include query terms, rate limits, and output fields for downstream analysis.

output_examples.output: A concise gene summary with Gene ID 672, symbol BRCA1, organism Homo sapiens, chromosome 17, and map location.

output_examples.input: Annotate a list of human oncology genes.
output_examples.output: A table-ready summary describing each matched gene, unmatched symbols, and any lookup errors.
A structured narrative covering aliases, chromosomal location, gene type, and transcript examples.

best_practices: Specify organism for every symbol search.
Use Gene IDs when precision matters.
Cache repeated results and follow NCBI rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not treat gene annotations as clinical guidance.
Do not batch large lists without rate limiting.
Do not paste private API keys into shared transcripts or logs.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. NCBI API keys are optional, but they increase request limits for larger workloads.

faq.question: Which APIs does it use?
faq.answer: It documents and scripts NCBI E-utilities and the NCBI Datasets Gene API.

faq.question: Can it process many genes at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch script accepts comma-separated Gene IDs or a file of gene symbols.

faq.question: Does it provide medical interpretation?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves reference gene data and should not be used as medical advice.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The scripts can print readable summaries or JSON output for downstream tools.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.
